docs: fix small errors in the 2026-07-28 and draft specification (#3586)

Fixes items b to i of #3491 in the 2026-07-28 and draft versions. Item a
was fixed in #3516, so this closes the issue. No requirement changes.

Fixes #3491

- **b)** The "Client Features" card on the specification index links to
the elicitation page. Its old target does not exist.
- **c)** The "Refresh Tokens" reference uses `draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-13`,
like the other OAuth 2.1 references.
- **d)** The changelog item on `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` lists
`server/discover` (2026-07-28 only, because the draft changelog does not
carry this item).
- **e)** The form schema text says which property types are allowed, and
that the only arrays are multi-select enums. The
`PrimitiveSchemaDefinition` comment in `schema.ts` says the same.
- **f)** The URL mode diagram shows `mode` and `url` inside the
elicitation request, not as fields of `InputRequiredResult`.
- **g)** The Sampling "Messages" section says `content` can be one block
or an array, and includes tool use and tool result content.
- **h)** The `list_changed` examples include
`io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId`. The resources page names the
stream that `list_changed` is sent on.
- **i)** The compatibility matrix has the two missing rows: a modern
client and a dual-era client, each with a dual-era server.

Checked locally: formatting, schema, schema pages, examples, and SEP
pages. The link check and `schema.json` generation were not run locally,
so `schema.json` was edited by hand to match `schema.ts`.

commit.message:
docs: mark Skills support for Claude and Claude Code in the extension matrix (#3588)

Marks Claude (web) and Claude Code as supporting the [Skills over
MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/skills/overview)
extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/skills`) in the extension support
matrix.

Skills over MCP entered public beta in Claude and Claude Code on
2026-11-24: [MCP servers can now ship skills, run tasks, and more with
Claude](https://claude.com/resources/articles/skills-over-mcp-tasks-and-more).
Claude Code requires v2.1.331 or later
([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp#use-skills-from-mcp-servers)).

Claude Desktop is left unmarked. The Claude Code docs list Desktop
connectors and Desktop extensions as unsupported.

commit.message:
docs: fix small errors in the 2026-07-28 and draft docs (#3587)

Fixes small errors found in a sweep of the docs, in the 2026-07-28 and
draft versions. The changelog edits are in 2026-07-28 only.

**Please look at these:**

- Caching: the page now says that `notifications/resources/updated` is
the relevant notification for a cached `resources/read` result. The
existing rule only says "a relevant notification". SEP-2549 pairs the
two, but this sentence is new in a released version.
- Dynamic Client Registration: the deprecation notice gives the version,
the PR, and the twelve-month period from the feature lifecycle policy.
- Elicitation: "**MUST** include the following parameters" now says that
form mode requests **MAY** omit `mode`, because `mode` is optional in
the schema.
- Resources: there is a new Resource Template field list, taken from the
schema.
- Kotlin: the client and server guides need JDK 17, because the SDK's
samples require it.

**Specification:**

- Mark optional fields as optional in tools, completion, and resources.
- Use one metadata URL in the Client ID Metadata Document diagram.
- Fix links to extensions and Skills, and the list of utilities on the
index page.
- Say what `includeContext` does, and fix a request ID in the Sampling
diagram.
- Say that the progress example leaves out required `_meta` fields.
- In draft, the Roots, Sampling, and Logging notices refer to the
release of the revision that deprecated them.

**Guides:**

- Link to the matching specification version, not `latest`.
- Use the error messages that the SDKs print, and correct the commands
and jar names.
- Say that clients need a `subscriptions/listen` stream to receive
`notifications/tools/list_changed`.
- Add alt text to the introduction diagram.

Checked locally: formatting, schema, schema pages, examples, and SEP
pages. The Python, TypeScript, and Ruby error messages come from running
the SDKs. For Kotlin, only the SDK source was read. The link check was
not run locally.

docs(blog): celebrate two years of MCP (#3584)

## Summary

Adds the blog post for the second anniversary of MCP, with an animated
header, images, and a quote from Angie Jones. It looks back at the year
through the people building on MCP and the community that shapes it.

Merging publishes the post right away.

This stays a draft until the author completes the contribution
disclosure.

compatibility shims), and `npm run prep`.

commit.message:
docs(community): align IG charters with SEP sponsorship guidelines (#3531)

<!-- claude-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **David Soria Parra** · [Slack
thread](https://ant-mcp-oss.slack.com/archives/C0BDGKP4PC6/p1794253161846999)_

**Before:** The Authorization IG charter said SEP sponsorship remains
with Maintainers and Core Maintainers and that a proposer "finds a
sponsor". The Financial Services IG charter said SEPs move toward the
core specification "with core-maintainer sponsorship". Both predate the
working-group-first SEP process in #3529.

**After:** Both charters say SEP sponsorship follows the [SEP
guidelines](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/community/sep-guidelines).
The Authorization IG charter keeps its single-venue model, including
that the IG does not charter a sub-group per topic and that a separate
working group is the exception. Acceptance stays with Maintainers and
Core Maintainers. Each charter gets a 2026-11-10 Changelog row.

How: Two sentences in `docs/community/interest-groups/auth.mdx` (Out of
Scope, and the problem-pitch paragraph) and one bullet in
`docs/community/interest-groups/financial-services.mdx` now point to the
SEP guidelines, plus a Changelog row in each. `npm run prep` passes.
This complements #3529, which updates the SEP guidelines themselves.
Charter amendments need Core Maintainer approval under [Amending or
retiring a
group](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/community/working-interest-groups#amending-or-retiring-a-group),
so this needs a Core Maintainer review.

This PR was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code).

commit.message:
docs(community): add Core Primitives WG charter (#3545)

<!-- claude-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **David Soria Parra** · [Slack
thread](https://ant-mcp-oss.slack.com/archives/C0BDGKP4PC6/p1793975038956449)_

Follow-up to #3513. Follows #3544.

**Before:** The Core Primitives WG has leads, a repository and a weekly
meeting. It has no charter page, nav entry or Current groups line.

**After:** The group has a charter built from the [charter
template](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/ddbbf0f8ab3038a3406844e9ee063644eae57cc3/docs/community/charter-template.mdx)
with only sourced content, a nav entry under Working Groups, and a
Current groups line. Sections with no source say "To be confirmed" or
"To be defined by the leads". Membership is omitted, as the template
allows until the group has members. The overview row now links the
charter.

## Sources

- **Mission and In Scope:** the group's three problem statements, which
David pointed to in review and in the Slack thread. The tool result
shape statement is under review in
modelcontextprotocol/core-primitives-wg#2. The stability and audience
statements are working documents and are not linked here. The primitive
annotations item and the open-scope statement come from the roadmap
([roadmap.mdx
L65-L77](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/ddbbf0f8ab3038a3406844e9ee063644eae57cc3/docs/development/roadmap.mdx#L65-L77),
[L22](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/ddbbf0f8ab3038a3406844e9ee063644eae57cc3/docs/development/roadmap.mdx#L22)).
- **Out of Scope:** progressive discovery is handled by the Progressive
Disclosure WG, per David's [review
comment](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/3545#discussion_r4542588810).
- **Related Groups:** the File Uploads WG line in the same priority area
([L77](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/ddbbf0f8ab3038a3406844e9ee063644eae57cc3/docs/development/roadmap.mdx#L77))
and the progressive discovery item
([L74](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/ddbbf0f8ab3038a3406844e9ee063644eae57cc3/docs/development/roadmap.mdx#L74)),
now handled by the Progressive Disclosure WG.
- **Leads:** the `core-primitives-wg-leads` team in Access ([roles.ts
L418-L428](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/access/blob/f89698a2e3206656d464c2ca203279cd1695ca4c/src/config/roles.ts#L418-L428))
with members
[kurtisvg](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/access/blob/f89698a2e3206656d464c2ca203279cd1695ca4c/src/config/users.ts#L582-L594)
and
[dsp-ant](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/access/blob/f89698a2e3206656d464c2ca203279cd1695ca4c/src/config/users.ts#L312-L335),
added by modelcontextprotocol/access#172 and
modelcontextprotocol/access#234.
- **Organizations:** Google for Kurtis from the Progressive Disclosure
charter (`docs/community/working-groups/progressive-disclosure.mdx`,
line 70), Anthropic for David from the Server Card charter
(`docs/community/working-groups/server-card.mdx`, line 38).
- **Operations:** the weekly 60 minute meeting on the [community
calendar](https://meet.modelcontextprotocol.io/tag/core-primitives-wg),
the [core-primitives-wg
repository](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/core-primitives-wg),
and the [Discord
channel](https://discord.com/channels/1358869848138059966/1540127738080534648)
that the calendar events link. The Discord API returns the name
`core-primitives-wg` for that channel id.
- **Authority & Decision Rights:** the template default table in
`docs/community/charter-template.mdx`, unchanged.
- **Active Work Items:** the three current focus items. Status and
champion for shape and stability come from the status and contributor
lines of their problem statements. The audience statement names neither.
No source gives target dates.
- **Overview row:** the row added by #3544 now links the charter.

## Questions for @kurtisvg and @dsp-ant

1. **Mission:** the wording here paraphrases the roadmap.
modelcontextprotocol/core-primitives-wg#1 is open and proposes a README
sentence. Confirm this wording or replace it?
2. **Progressive discovery:** answered in review. It is out of scope and
handled by the Progressive Disclosure WG.
3. **Extra scope:** partly answered in review. Tool Result Stability and
Tool Result Audience are now in scope. Two points remain. The notes also
list Resource Link Traversal with no owner. Is it in scope? Primitive
annotations stays in scope as a roadmap item outside the current focus.
Keep it there or remove it?
4. **Out of Scope:** partly answered in review. Progressive discovery is
listed. Does anything else belong there?
5. **Members:** Access lists only the two leads.
modelcontextprotocol/core-primitives-wg#1 proposes Kyle Rubenok, Luca
Chang and Kryspin Ziemski. Who are the members, with organization,
Discord handle and level?
6. **Leadership:** no source gives the lead terms. What are they?
7. **Sponsorship:** the template requires the group to be sponsored
under "Forming a group" in `docs/community/working-interest-groups.mdx`.
Who sponsored it?
8. **Operations:** is there an Office Hours slot, and should the charter
link the meeting notes document?
9. **Work items:** status and champion for shape and stability now come
from the problem statements. Who champions the audience item, and what
are the SEP numbers and target dates? The notes say "March Spec" for
most items. For success criteria, the notes list a definition of done:
SEP, reference implementation, guidance and documentation updates.
10. **Authority table:** it is the template default. Should any row
change?
11. **Naming:** Access spells the member role singular
(`core-primitive-wg`, from modelcontextprotocol/access#172) and every
other source is plural. Should Access be renamed?

This PR was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code).

---------

Co-authored-by: Den Delimarsky <hi@den.dev>
Co-authored-by: Den <53200638+localden@users.noreply.github.com>

Tool Result Audience are now in scope. Two points remain. The notes also
list Resource Link Traversal with no owner. Is it in scope? Primitive
annotations stays in scope as a roadmap item outside the current focus.
Keep it there or remove it?
4. **Out of Scope:** partly answered in review. Progressive discovery is
listed. Does anything else belong there?
5. **Members:** Access lists only the two leads.
modelcontextprotocol/core-primitives-wg#1 proposes Kyle Rubenok, Luca
Chang and Kryspin Ziemski. Who are the members, with organization,
Discord handle and level?
6. **Leadership:** no source gives the lead terms. What are they?
7. **Sponsorship:** the template requires the group to be sponsored
under "Forming a group" in `docs/community/working-interest-groups.mdx`.
Who sponsored it?
8. **Operations:** is there an Office Hours slot, and should the charter
link the meeting notes document?
9. **Work items:** status and champion for shape and stability now come
from the problem statements. Who champions the audience item, and what
are the SEP numbers and target dates? The notes say "March Spec" for
most items. For success criteria, the notes list a definition of done:
SEP, reference implementation, guidance and documentation updates.
10. **Authority table:** it is the template default. Should any row
change?
11. **Naming:** Access spells the member role singular
(`core-primitive-wg`, from modelcontextprotocol/access#172) and every
other source is plural. Should Access be renamed?

commit.message:
docs: add VS Code to Skills extension column in client matrix (#3510)

Marks VS Code GitHub Copilot as supporting the [Skills over
MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/skills/overview)
extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/skills`) in the extension support
matrix.

Support shipped in VS Code 1.147: [Skills over MCP are now available in
VS
Code](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/azuredevcommunityblog/skills-over-mcp-are-now-available-in-vs-code/4574580).
The `chat.agentHost.mcpSkills.enabled` setting defaults to `true`
(microsoft/vscode at `f26893c248a`).

Implementation:
[microsoft/vscode#345956](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/345956)
(agentHost: support skills served by MCP servers).

Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
